problemStatement.formal: R(4,k) bounds: Omega(k^{5/2}/polylog) <= R(4,k) <= O(k^3/(log k)^2)
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the classical Ramsey upper bound R(r,s) <= C(r+s-2, r-1), prove structural properties, and state the key probabilistic bounds for R(3,k) and R(4,k).
whyMatters: The R(4,k) problem is a major open problem in Ramsey theory
The gap between k^{5/2} and k^3 lower/upper bounds remains unresolved
Probabilistic method bounds are foundational in combinatorics

proven: Ramsey upper bound R(r,s) <= C(r+s-2, r-1) via binomial coefficients
Base cases: R(1,s) = R(r,1) = 1, R(0,s) = R(r,0) = 0
Monotonicity: R(r,s) <= R(r+1,s) and R(r,s) <= R(r,s+1)
Pascal recursive bound: R(r,s) = R(r-1,s) + R(r,s-1)
Pred corollaries: R(r,s) >= R(r-1,s) and R(r,s) >= R(r,s-1)
open: Exact order of growth of R(4,k): between k^{5/2} and k^3 (up to log factors)
AKS R(3,k) = O(k^2/log k) upper bound (axiomatized)
Kim R(3,k) = Omega(k^2/log k) lower bound (axiomatized)
knownResults.goal: Complete formalization with 16 proved theorems and 5 axioms for deep probabilistic results

currentState.focus: Structural properties of the Ramsey upper bound function
blockers: Probabilistic method proofs require Lovasz Local Lemma and random graph models not yet in Mathlib
currentState.nextAction: Consider converting axioms to theorem sorries for Aristotle submission

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: RamseyR4kExtensions.lean now has 22 proved theorems (0 sorries) and 5 axioms. Added Pascal recursive bound R(r,s) = R(r-1,s) + R(r,s-1), verified for small cases, and proved pred corollaries.
builtItems: ramseyUpperBound_pascal: R(r,s) = R(r-1,s) + R(r,s-1) via Nat.choose_succ_succ
insights: Nat.choose_symm signature: (hk : k <= n) -> C(n, n-k) = C(n, k) - careful with Nat subtraction
Nat.choose_le_choose enables monotonicity: C(n, k) <= C(n+1, k)
Nat.choose_pos gives positivity: C(n, k) > 0 when k <= n
native_decide works well for small concrete Ramsey bound computations
Probabilistic method proofs are fundamentally blocked by missing Mathlib infrastructure
The R(4,k) gap (k^{5/2} vs k^3) is an active research problem
Nat.choose_succ_succ gives Pascal rule: C(n+1, k+1) = C(n, k) + C(n, k+1)
Pascal rule enables both recursive computation and proving R(r,s) >= R(r-1,s)

No probabilistic method for combinatorics in Mathlib
